title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is a very faint image, which looks like an offset or ghost of the preceding page 74, not an independent text. The layout matches page 74 line for line, and the image confirms most of that page's readable content: 'dont la deuxième est donnée par (41) [ρ1 ↦ σ∞, ρ∞ ↦ ρ^{-1}] ρ0=(ρ∞ρ1)^{-1} ↦ … = ε0 (or τ0), et la première par (42) [τ… ↦ τ∞], …, [τ∞ ↦ τ∞]'. The sketches are the same too: a spherical triangle with vertices 0, 1, ∞ and the tetrahedron-on-pentagon figure. So are the lists 'π_{D_n}, π_{S4^+}, π_{S4}, π_{S5^+}', 'π_X → X une carte : on oublie les sommets', 'π_icos, π_dodéc, π_tétr, π_cube, π_oct' and 'π_pavages, π_P → polygone combinatoire fini'.

Mathematically, Grothendieck is writing out how generators transform under two automorphisms or transitions. The generators are ρ0, ρ1, ρ∞, with ρ0ρ1ρ∞ = 1, generating the cartographic/triangle group of the projective line minus {0,1,∞}, together with the elements σ, τ. The two automorphisms would be the S3 symmetries of {0,1,∞} acting on the oriented cartographic group. He then lists the fundamental groupoids attached to combinatorial maps (cartes) with finite symmetry groups. These are the dihedral groups, the tetrahedral/octahedral group S4 and the icosahedral group A5 = S5^+. They correspond to the Platonic solids, regular tilings (pavages) and polygons, with the remark that a carte gives a covering π_X → X.

The purpose is to build a catalogue of 'Teichmüller-type' groupoids attached to the regular spherical maps. These serve as test cases and building blocks for the Teichmüller tower and for the S0 T_{g,ν} constructions of the dossier. The next page starts on the combinatorics of the dodecahedron: 120 flags (repères), 12 faces, 30 edges, 20 vertices.
